title: The Fair share of the money
subtitle: 责任担当 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 责任担当（做人与做事·责任与担当）
meta: 主题语境：责任担当（做人与做事·责任与担当）　|　核心词汇：fair　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 fair 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 the warden wrote of ① a fair share of the money in the register, and everybody in the centre said at once that it was ② fairer than the one named there the year before. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the warden, who never explained anything, had done it with great care and gone home; it was the fair ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the fairest share of the money anybody in the centre had ever seen, or so the register for June 1942 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too fair to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the resident who had come to help; the fair ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the notice at the far gate, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a fair day for the market, and said that no resident in his right mind would call it ⑥ as fair as the day for the market they had once had in the old centre. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was fair or not, and he said so.

By 1955 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the register. What the line asked for was ⑦ something fair, and nothing besides. The resident from the next centre called the whole plan ⑧ quite fair; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the register kept the names of the fair ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1958, on the same day, she wrote of another fair share of the money in the same register, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ fairer than anybody had expected. ⑩ The fairest day for the market in the whole centre, she said in 1960, was the one she could never quite name; the fair ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 公平（前置定语 a fair share of the money：1948 年管理员在登记册里记下的那件公平的那份钱）
B. adj. 公平／晴朗（比较级 fairer than：文中两处，一处比均分的那份钱，一处比预想）
C. adj. 公平／晴朗（最高级 the fairest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 公平（表语 too fair to do：母亲觉得它太公平，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 晴朗（前置定语 a fair day for the market：叔叔把整件事称作一桩晴朗的好天气）
F. adj. 晴朗（同级比较 as fair as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩集市那天的好天气相比）
G. adj. 晴朗（后置定语 something fair：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 晴朗（受程度副词修饰 quite fair：那位居民的评价）

items.q: a fair share of the money
the fairest share of the money anybody
a fair day for the market
The fairest day for the market in

answers.why: fair 意为“公平”，1948 年管理员在登记册里记下的是“一件公平的那份钱”，此处作前置定语 a fair share of the money。
fair 意为“公平”，此处用比较级 fairer than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
fair 意为“公平”，登记册上 六月 那行字说它是社区中心里最公平的一件，故用最高级 the fairest share of the money。
fair 意为“公平”，母亲认为这件东西“太公平了，谁也用不上”，too fair to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
fair 意为“晴朗”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩晴朗的好天气”，此处作前置定语 a fair day for the market。
fair 意为“晴朗”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩集市那天的好天气一样晴朗”，同级比较用 as fair as。
fair 意为“晴朗”，登记册上那半行字要的是“晴朗的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something fair。
fair 意为“晴朗”，邻社区中心来的那位居民认为这套计划“相当晴朗”，quite 修饰原级 fair。
fair 意为“晴朗”，1958 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要晴朗”，故用比较级 fairer than。
fair 意为“晴朗”，母亲 1960 年说的是“整个社区中心里最晴朗的那一桩”，故用最高级 the fairest day for the market。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1948 年，管理员在登记册里记下了一件公平的那份钱。（a fair share of the money）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更公平。（fairer than …）
母亲觉得它太公平，谁也用不上。（too fair to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩晴朗的好天气。（a fair day for the market）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩集市那天的好天气一样晴朗。（as fair as …）
到了 1955 年，登记册上只剩半行字：要的是一件晴朗的东西。（something fair）
answers: In 1948 the warden wrote of a fair share of the money in the register.
Everybody said it was fairer than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too fair to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a fair day for the market.
He said nobody would call it as fair as the day for the market they had once had.
By 1955 the register asked for nothing but something fair.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 fair 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1948 the warden wrote of a fair share of the money in the register, and nobody forgot it.
It was the fairest share of the money in the centre, or so the register says.
My mother thought it too fair to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a fair day for the market, and nobody argued with him.
The resident from the next centre called the plan quite fair, and everybody laughed.
The fair ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
